answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, turning identity creation from free into costly. The stake is a haven only for honest actors: good behavior earns it back, fraud forfeits it, so one operator spinning up thousands of sock puppets must fund each one. Reputation accrues per staked identity over a long voyage of verified deals, and newcomers start on a narrow ledge with tiny trade limits that widen only as their history proves honest. Attackers pay real capital per fake identity; honest agents compound trust cheaply.
